newsitem.title: USA: GM mulls appeal of attorney fees in settlement.
newsitem.headline: GM mulls appeal of attorney fees in settlement.

text.p: General Motors Corp is considering filing an appeal in the wake of a Louisiana judge's approval of a multi-million-dollar settlement of a class-action lawsuit against the automaker.

The judge last week gave final approval to a plan that would end a three-year legal battle on behalf of owners of as many as 5.8 million of the company's C/K pickup trucks. The trucks, sold during the model years 1973-1987, have side-mounted fuel tanks that allegedly made them unsafe in some types of collisions.

The settlement, which won preliminary approval in July, calls for GM to provide $1,000 coupons to each of the more than five million C/K pickup owners and pay about $28 million in fees and expenses to the plaintiffs' attorneys.
"We're evaluating the judge's order," said Ed Lechtzin, a GM spokesman, "and considering an appeal of only the attorney fees, not the ruling concerning the certificates."
Ironically, the settlement may also be challenged by a group of dissident plaintiffs, although Lechtzin said any such action by that group would have nothing to do with GM's potential appeal.
Lechtzin also said it remains unclear when the certificates will be passed out.

"If there's no appeal (by the dissident plaitiffs or by GM), the court order would take effect within 70 days," he explained. "We would then notify truck owners and they would have to provide proof of ownership (of the affected vehicles) as of July 4, 1996."
Some of the trucks involved are 23 years old, and the automaker could possibly reap sales benefits by handing out the certificates to owners of the older pickups.
